title: Model admission playbook for enterprise onboarding, version pins, and deprecations
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Purpose: Create a concise, operational playbook to triage and prioritize enterprise model catalog requests (new model adds, version pin requests, and model deprecations). The playbook will translate ad-hoc customer asks into consistent outcomes: accepted+onboarded, accepted+deferred (with timeline), rejected (with rationale), or escalated to security/compliance. Background: Enterprise customers frequently request specific model variants or version pins to meet regulatory SLAs or to avoid regression. Current intake is inconsistent across PMs and leads to surprise regressions and support load. Scope: intake form fields, scoring rubric, SME review criteria, mandatory eval-gates and pass thresholds, rollout recommendations (canary/AB rollback), owner handoff checklist, communications templates for customers, and metrics to track throughput and post-onboard regressions. Out of scope: implementation of the runtime-side quantization pipeline (ENG owns). Stakeholders: PMs (onboarding lead), Runtime engineering (serving + eval infra), Applied ML (quality signatures & evals), Security & Compliance, Customer Success. Expected outcomes: faster decisions (TTR target 7 days), fewer post-onboard regressions, clear audit trail for enterprise decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A documented playbook published to Confluence with versioning and owner (link placeholder: https://confluence.redwood.example/model-admission-playbook)

A standardized intake form created in Zendesk/Forms capturing required attributes: customer use-case, SLA, PII class, requested model + variant, reason for pin/deprecate, expected traffic, and urgency
A weighted prioritization rubric defined (weights for customer SLA, security/regulatory, cost delta, latency change, eval-signal delta) and a sample scoring worksheet
Mandatory eval-gates defined with pass/fail thresholds for accuracy/regression/ toxicity and defined fallback actions
A review rotation schedule and RACI with Applied ML and Runtime SMEs assigned
Playbook reviewed and sign-off from Security & Compliance and Customer Success
A small pilot run: triage 3 real incoming enterprise requests using the playbook and document outcomes/lessons
triage_flow: Step 1 - Intake: customer fills standardized form; ticket created in Linear with tag 'model-intake'
Step 2 - Auto-classify: PM scoring bot fills preliminary rubric fields from form (owner: PM)
Step 3 - PM review: PM validates classification and assigns to SME pool if score >= threshold
Step 4 - Eval gating: Applied ML runs predefined eval suite (latency, perf on cust prompts, safety scans). If fails, action: reject or request mitigation plan
Step 5 - Security check: for requests with PII/regulatory scope, Security performs accelerated review
Step 6 - Decision: Accept to onboard (planned release, rollout plan), Accept but defer (with committed timeline), Reject (document reason), or Escalate
Step 7 - Onboarding checklist: infra quota, model artifacts uploaded, variant mapping, QA tests, rollout plan with canary percentages and rollback criteria
Step 8 - Communication: standardized customer update templates and internal post-mortem if regression occurs
scoring_rubric_summary: Customer SLA impact (weight 30): Does customer require exact deterministic pins for compliance/validated outputs?
Security/Compliance risk (weight 25): Does the model handle regulated data or require encryption/HSM?
Operational cost delta (weight 15): Estimated token cost or GPU footprint delta relative to our recommended baseline
Latency/regression risk (weight 15): Estimated change to 95th pct latency or likelihood of quality regression
Eval-signal delta (weight 15): delta in eval pass rate against our canonical prompt set (safety, accuracy, hallucination)
Score interpretation: >=80 accept; 60-79 review with SMEs; <60 reject or request mitigation
rollout_recommendations: Small enterprise onboard: start with 5% canary for 48hrs, monitor token-level cost, latency, and quality-signal dashboards
High-risk/regulatory: require dedicated test harness with customer-provided prompts and a 14-day run before production
Version pinned customer migration: offer a migration window and a pinned fallback route for 90 days
Deprecation: provide 60-day notice, recommended replacement mapping, and regression guardrails for customer fallbacks
metrics_and_kpis: % of onboarded models that trigger post-onboard regression incident (target < 5%)
Average rubric score distribution and correlation to post-onboard issues
Number of enterprise requests triaged per month and backlog growth rate
open_questions: Do we need a hard SLA for triage decisions for enterprise customers or just an internal target?
Can runtime instrumentation produce a standardized latency delta estimate pre-onboard? (ENG input required)
Should we require customers to provide a representative prompt set as part of intake?
Where will canonical eval suites live and who owns maintenance? (Applied ML ask)
What is the approach for billing changes when a customer requests a higher-cost model variant?
implementation_notes: Work with Platform Eng to add 'model-intake' template to Linear and map form fields to ticket properties
Build a lightweight rubric spreadsheet that can be auto-populated by a PM script; ENG to provide latency estimate API
Applied ML to author initial eval suite and safety checks; Security to provide checklist for regulated data
Customer Success to prepare 3 communication templates: accepted, deferred, rejected
Pilot the playbook with two current enterprise onboarding requests slated in Feb and collect feedback
